text.headline: Zong-Liang Yang, Ph.D. - Research Chronicle
text.text: A timeline of academic training, research innovations, and scientific contributions to climate science.

text.headline: M.S. in Meteorology
text.text: Completed Master's degree in Meteorology at University of Melbourne, Australia.

text.headline: Ph.D. Studies Begin
text.text: Started doctoral research in Atmospheric Sciences at Macquarie University, Sydney.

text.headline: Ph.D. Completed
text.text: Earned Ph.D. in Atmospheric Sciences from Macquarie University.

text.headline: University of Arizona
text.text: Postdoctoral researcher and then research faculty at University of Arizona.

text.headline: Joins UT Austin Faculty
text.text: Appointed to faculty in Department of Geological Sciences at University of Texas at Austin.

text.headline: Joseph C. Walter Jr. Excellence Award
text.text: Received the most prestigious internal award in the Jackson School of Geosciences.

text.headline: NCAR CCSM Distinguished Achievement Award
text.text: Shared NCAR 2008 CCSM Distinguished Achievement Award for contributions to climate modeling.

text.headline: Co-Chair of NCAR Land Working Group
text.text: Appointed Co-Chair of the NCAR Community Climate System Model Land Working Group.

text.headline: Noah-MP Model Published
text.text: Published landmark papers on the Community Noah Land Surface Model with Multi-Parameterization Options.

text.headline: Hurricane Harvey Forecasting
text.text: Yang's Noah-MP model proved critical in accurately forecasting Hurricane Harvey's extreme rainfall and flooding impacts.

text.headline: Jackson Chair in Earth System Sciences
text.text: Holds the John A. and Katherine G. Jackson Chair in Earth System Sciences at UT Austin.

text.headline: Elected AGU Fellow
text.text: Elected as American Geophysical Union Fellow for exemplary leadership and outstanding scientific achievements in land surface interactions and climate modeling.
